cases.french: J'ai assisté à la réunion ce matin.
cases.reference_english: I attended the meeting this morning.
must_mention: assister à means to attend / be present at

cases.french: Ma librairie préférée est près du lac.
cases.reference_english: My favourite bookshop is near the lake.

cases.french: Mon fils est très sensible.
cases.reference_english: My son is very sensitive.

cases.french: Actuellement, je travaille sur une application.
cases.reference_english: Currently, I'm working on an app.

cases.french: Éventuellement, nous irons à Annecy.
cases.reference_english: We might possibly go to Annecy.

cases.french: Elle a demandé l'addition.
cases.reference_english: She asked for the bill.

cases.french: Je vais rester à l'hôtel ce soir.
cases.reference_english: I'm going to stay at the hotel tonight.

cases.french: Demain, je passe un examen.
cases.reference_english: Tomorrow I'm taking an exam.
must_mention: passer un examen = to take / sit an exam
must_not_say: says the speaker passed / will pass

cases.french: J'ai hâte de voir le mont Blanc.
cases.reference_english: I can't wait to see Mont Blanc.
must_mention: avoir hâte de = can't wait to / look forward to (eagerness)
must_not_say: says it means being in a hurry

cases.french: Il pleut des cordes.
cases.reference_english: It's pouring.

cases.french: Mon ami m'a posé un lapin.
cases.reference_english: My friend stood me up.
must_mention: poser un lapin = to stand someone up
must_not_say: mentions an actual rabbit as the meaning

cases.french: Ce n'est pas la mer à boire.
cases.reference_english: It's not that hard.
must_mention: idiom: it's not a huge task / not that difficult

cases.french: J'ai la flemme d'aller courir.
cases.reference_english: I can't be bothered to go running.
must_mention: avoir la flemme = can't be bothered

cases.french: Elle est tombée dans les pommes.
cases.reference_english: She fainted.
must_mention: tomber dans les pommes = to faint

cases.french: J'ai le cafard depuis lundi.
cases.reference_english: I've been feeling down since Monday.
must_mention: avoir le cafard = to feel down / blue

cases.french: Tu veux un thé ?
cases.reference_english: Do you want some tea?

cases.french: Vous voulez un thé ?
cases.reference_english: Would you like some tea?

cases.french: Je voudrais un thé, s'il vous plaît.
cases.reference_english: I'd like a tea, please.
must_mention: voudrais = conditional of vouloir, used for politeness

cases.french: Ça marche !
cases.reference_english: Sounds good! / Okay!

cases.french: C'est pas grave.
cases.reference_english: No worries. / It's no big deal.
must_mention: standard form: ce n'est pas grave
must_not_say: calls it incorrect French without mentioning it's normal speech
cases.note: Checker may flag the dropped ne, which locks Explain. Decide whether everyday spoken French should unlock.

cases.french: Ouais, c'est sympa.
cases.reference_english: Yeah, it's nice.

cases.french: Quand j'étais petit, je jouais au basket.
cases.reference_english: When I was little, I used to play basketball.
must_mention: imparfait for a past habit / background
must_not_say: calls it a single past event

cases.french: Il pleuvait quand je suis arrivé.
cases.reference_english: It was raining when I arrived.
must_mention: passé composé = the event that happened
must_not_say: treats both verbs as the same tense

cases.french: J'ai habité à Lyon pendant deux ans.
cases.reference_english: I lived in Lyon for two years.
must_not_say: says the speaker still lives there

cases.french: J'habite à Seattle depuis dix ans.
cases.reference_english: I've lived in Seattle for ten years.

cases.french: Je viens de finir mon thé.
cases.reference_english: I've just finished my tea.
must_mention: venir de + infinitive = just did (recent past)

cases.french: Je suis en train de lire.
cases.reference_english: I'm reading (right now).
must_mention: être en train de = in the middle of doing

cases.french: Nous allons partir demain.
cases.reference_english: We're going to leave tomorrow.

cases.french: Nous partirons demain.
cases.reference_english: We will leave tomorrow.
must_mention: both futures are correct; near future is more conversational
must_not_say: says one of the two futures is wrong

cases.french: Si j'avais le temps, j'irais à Chamonix.
cases.reference_english: If I had time, I'd go to Chamonix.
must_not_say: says it's about a real past situation

cases.french: J'aurais dû partir plus tôt.
cases.reference_english: I should have left earlier.
must_mention: past conditional of devoir = should have
must_not_say: translates as 'I would have had to'

cases.french: Il faut que tu viennes ce soir.
cases.reference_english: You have to come tonight.
must_mention: viennes is the subjunctive of venir
must_not_say: calls viennes a typo or present tense

cases.french: Je cherche un hôtel qui soit calme.
cases.reference_english: I'm looking for a hotel that's quiet (any one).
must_mention: subjunctive in the relative clause = no specific hotel yet
qui est calme would mean a specific hotel

cases.french: Il entra dans la pièce et ferma la porte.
cases.reference_english: He came into the room and closed the door.
must_mention: passé simple, used in written narrative
spoken equivalent: il est entré, il a fermé

cases.french: Elle fut très surprise.
cases.reference_english: She was very surprised.
must_not_say: says fut is the future tense

cases.french: Ils allèrent au marché.
cases.reference_english: They went to the market.

cases.french: Elle prit son manteau et sortit.
cases.reference_english: She took her coat and went out.
must_mention: prit (prendre) and sortit (sortir) are passé simple

cases.french: Bien qu'il fût tard, ils continuèrent.
cases.reference_english: Although it was late, they carried on.
must_mention: modern French: bien qu'il soit tard

cases.french: Il ne parlait guère.
cases.reference_english: He hardly spoke.

cases.french: Partez avant qu'il ne pleuve.
cases.reference_english: Leave before it rains.
must_mention: this ne is not negative (ne explétif)

cases.french: Samedi, je vais au parc.
cases.reference_english: This Saturday, I'm going to the park.

cases.french: Le samedi, je vais au parc.
cases.reference_english: On Saturdays, I go to the park.

cases.french: Je mange du fromage, mais j'aime surtout le chèvre.
cases.reference_english: I eat cheese, but I especially like goat's cheese.
must_mention: le chèvre = goat's cheese (la chèvre = the goat)

cases.french: Je n'ai pas de voiture.
cases.reference_english: I don't have a car.
must_mention: after a negation, un/une becomes de

cases.french: Ma femme est médecin.
cases.reference_english: My wife is a doctor.
must_mention: no article before a profession after être

cases.french: Je pense à toi.
cases.reference_english: I'm thinking of you.
must_mention: penser à = to think about someone/something

cases.french: Que penses-tu de ce film ?
cases.reference_english: What do you think of this film?
must_mention: penser de = to have an opinion about

cases.french: Nous allons en France, au Canada et aux États-Unis.
cases.reference_english: We're going to France, Canada and the United States.
must_not_say: treats the three prepositions as interchangeable

cases.french: Des pommes ? J'en ai deux.
cases.reference_english: Apples? I have two (of them).
must_mention: en replaces de + noun, needed with a number

cases.french: Je le lui ai donné.
cases.reference_english: I gave it to him / her.

cases.french: Donne-le-moi !
cases.reference_english: Give it to me!
must_mention: affirmative imperative: pronouns after the verb, with hyphens

cases.french: Je suis le guide jusqu'au refuge.
cases.reference_english: I'm following the guide to the hut.
must_mention: suis can be suivre (follow) or être (be)
here it most likely means follow
must_not_say: only says 'I am the guide' with no mention of the ambiguity

cases.french: Ce n'est pas mal du tout.
cases.reference_english: It's actually pretty good.

cases.french: Il y a pas mal de monde.
cases.reference_english: There are quite a lot of people.
must_mention: pas mal de = quite a lot of
cases.note: Also a checker false-alarm test: pas mal de is a quantifier and needs no ne.

cases.french: La tour est près du lac, mais le tour du lac est long.
cases.reference_english: The tower is near the lake, but the walk around the lake is long.
must_mention: le tour = tour / circuit; gender changes the meaning
must_not_say: treats tour as one word with one meaning

cases.french: On se fait la bise ?
cases.reference_english: Shall we greet with a kiss on the cheek?

cases.french: À tout à l'heure !
cases.reference_english: See you later (today)!
must_mention: compare à plus tard, à demain

cases.french: Je voudrais un aller-retour pour Annecy.
cases.reference_english: I'd like a return ticket to Annecy.
must_not_say: says it means going back and forth

cases.french: Le téléphérique est fermé à cause du vent.
cases.reference_english: The cable car is closed because of the wind.
must_mention: à cause de = because of (often a negative cause), du = de + le

cases.french: Il faut réserver le refuge à l'avance.
cases.reference_english: You have to book the mountain hut in advance.
must_mention: il faut + infinitive = it's necessary to / you have to
must_not_say: translates refuge as a refugee shelter

cases.french: Aujourd'hui, je porte des chaussures de course.
cases.reference_english: Today I'm wearing running shoes.
must_mention: je porte = I'm wearing / I wear (French has one present tense)
must_not_say: calls je porte a contraction or short for je suis portant
